title: I Followed the Distillery Tour Wristband Into the Barrel Room

parts.text: I paid the public tour at 1:15 p.m. and a staff guest in a paper band walked the barrel-room rope. The wristband chart at the door said: PUBLIC BAND = STILLHOUSE ONLY. BARREL ROOM = PAID ADD-ON. I was twenty-nine, gift-ticket holder, holding the add-on they said was sold out. Guide Rhea said, "Industry guests are the mash." I pointed at the chart. She winked. "Mash doesn't scan." I photographed the paper band past the rope, the chart, and my sold-out stub. Then I followed the same rope line with my public band and asked tasting to scan it. At 1:21 tasting asked why a public band was in the barrel room and why Rhea's guest was too.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Tasting can see a paper guest and a public band on the same barrel-room rope.

social.video_title: Industry guests skipped the barrel add-on — Part 1/2
social.description: Sold-out stub, a paper band past the rope, and a door chart. I asked them to scan me. Would you have stayed in the stillhouse?

parts.text: Rhea called it hospitality until the POS showed the add-on inventory. I printed the scans, the chart, and the photo. They sold me the add-on that was never sold out. Rhea’s guest bought a band. Optics is a word guides use when a rope has a camera. Tour policy now has a second line: MASH SCANS. I smell oak on a real ticket. Rhea counts add-ons. The barrel room finally has a till.

social.video_title: Mash scans at the barrel rope — Part 2/2
social.description: Inventory that was never sold out, a real add-on, and a second line on the chart. Was industry ever a paper band?
